target: Check what 'longer ones 0.7-1.3 mm' measures. In Chorizanthe the involucre teeth carry awns of two lengths, so 'awns absent' probably belongs to another variety, to the key, or to a different organ. The awn (PO:0025349) length may stand
fix: When '<part> absent' and a measurement such as 'longer ones X mm' come from the same taxon, the phrase 'longer ones' refers back to the nearest plural noun before it. Attach it to that noun. Read an absence inside a key lead or a variety paragraph as belonging to that lead or variety, not to the whole species.
reason: C. robusta normally has hooked awns on its involucre teeth. Without the full sentence it is impossible to tell which statement belongs to which form.

target: No absence at all. The phrase is about asexual propagules (gemma PO:0025614) and it reports a gap in the material. The leaf (PO:0025034) tubular annotation stands
fix: 'Specialized asexual reproduction not seen' or '<structure> not seen' is a note about the specimens, never an absence (PATO:0000462). If a phrase names no plant part, it must never be given a default part such as leaf. Drop it.
reason: 'Not seen' only says the material lacks something. 'Asexual reproduction' is a process, not the leaf.

target: stipel (PO:0020051) absent (PATO:0000462). The stipule (PO:0020051 is not the stipule) annotation 'persistent' stays on the stipule
fix: French 'stipelle(s)', 'stipellé', 'sans stipelles' and English 'stipel(s)', 'stipellate' map to stipel PO:0020051, never to stipule. A match on a longer word must take priority over its shorter prefix 'stipul-/stipel-'.
reason: Stipels (on the leaflets) and stipules are different organs. Dalbergia has stipules but no stipels.

target: stipel (PO:0020051) absent (PATO:0000462). The stipules are present and very small (decreased size PATO:0000587)
fix: 'sans stipelles' and 'stipelles absentes' map to stipel PO:0020051, never to stipule.
reason: Same error as X02252: the stipel was mapped to stipule.

target: bract (PO:0009055) present in some plants and absent in others. Record it as variable (context 'sometimes'), not as absent
fix: 'parfois absent(e)s', 'sometimes absent', 'often absent' and 'absent or ...' state that presence varies. They are never a taxon-wide absence. Keep the descriptions of the part when it is there.
reason: 'Parfois' (sometimes) makes this a variable presence, not an absence.

target: style (PO:0009074) absent only in the sterile ray flowers (ray flower PO:0025331). Disk flowers have a style. The pappus (PO:0025393) as a laciniate cupule is correct
fix: In Asteraceae, 'style absent', 'ovary sterile' and 'neutral' in the ray-floret paragraph belong to the ray flower PO:0025331. Keep the floret type as the context and never assert a taxon-wide absence.
reason: Aspilia rays are neutral. The pappus statement is about the achene of the disk flowers and does not conflict.

target: The external ostiolar bracts (at syconium ostiole FLOPO:0986063) are absent. The membranous bracts are the basal bracts of the fig (bract PO:0009055)
fix: In Ficus, 'sans bractées externes', 'external/ostiolar bracts absent' and 'without lateral bracts' refer to one kind of bract on the fig: ostiolar or lateral. Record the absence with that position as the context (syconium ostiole FLOPO:0986063). Never record a general 'bract absent' when basal bracts are also described.
reason: Figs have basal bracts, ostiolar bracts and sometimes lateral bracts. Lacking one kind does not mean lacking all bracts.

target: The external bracts of the syconium ostiole (FLOPO:0986063) are absent. The puberulous ones are the basal bracts (bract PO:0009055)
fix: Same rule as X02256: 'ostiole sans bractées externes' is an absence of ostiolar bracts only, with the ostiole as the context.
reason: The text itself names the ostiole as the place where the bracts are missing.

target: petal (PO:0009032) present and ciliate in some flowers, absent in others. Context 'sometimes'
fix: 'parfois absents' and 'sometimes absent' state that presence varies. Never record them as a taxon-wide absence.
reason: Scolopia petals vary in number and are sometimes missing. When present, they are ciliate.

target: leaf lamina (PO:0020039) absent only on the lower leaf sheaths (PO:0020104, context 'lower'). Upper leaves have a pubescent blade
fix: 'gaines inférieures sans limbe', 'bladeless sheaths' and 'lower leaves reduced to sheaths' describe the basal sheaths only. Keep the sheath and its position as the context. Never record a taxon-wide 'leaf lamina absent'.
reason: Sedges such as Scleria commonly have bladeless basal sheaths and bladed upper leaves. The KM notes record this same error on the moss flora.

target: lenticel (PO:0000031) absent on the branchlets (branch PO:0025073). The feminine 'lenticellée' is about another axis, probably the bark or stem (PO:0009047)
fix: 'non lenticellé(s)' and 'lenticellé(e)' must carry the part they agree with ('rameaux', 'écorce', 'tige'), including its grammatical gender and number. Lenticel absence and presence on different parts or at different ages are both true.
reason: The grammatical gender shows that the two statements describe different nouns.

target: lenticel (PO:0000031) absent on the young branchlets and present on the older branches (branch PO:0025073). Context: age or order of the branch
fix: In Strychnos, 'jeunes rameaux non lenticellés, rameaux âgés lenticellés' is a common pattern. Keep the branch age or order as the context of each statement, not the bare part.
reason: The usual reading is a difference by age. A slip in the flora is possible if both statements name the same twigs.

target: No leaf absence for the taxon. 'Without leaves' describes the inflorescence or flowering branch (inflorescence PO:0009049 not leafy). Leaves are present and paler olive or grey below
fix: 'without leaves' or 'leafless' that follows an inflorescence, panicle, flowering shoot or branchlet is about that axis only. Put the absence on that part, or drop it, and never record leaf absent for the whole taxon.
reason: The species clearly has leaves (their color is described). The phrase must belong to an axis.

target: Cystoliths absent in the leaf lamina (PO:0020039). There is no PO or FLOPO cystolith class, so drop it or queue cystolith as a FLOPO anatomy class. The lamina is present. 'Often not or only faintly branched' probably refers to hairs or veins, not to the lamina
fix: 'cystoliths absent', '<cell or inclusion> absent' and '<inclusion> present' never mean that the bearer (lamina, leaf) is absent. If no class exists for the named structure, drop the statement rather than move the absence to the bearer.
reason: Cystoliths are inclusions in the cells of the lamina. A taxon-wide lamina absence is impossible in Ficus.

target: Lateral bracts on the fig body are absent. The deflexed bracts are the basal bracts (bract PO:0009055)
fix: In Ficus, 'without lateral bracts' is an absence of the bracts on the fig wall only, with 'lateral, on the receptacle' as the context. Basal and ostiolar bracts are separate.
reason: Ficus descriptions separate basal, lateral and ostiolar bracts.

target: trichome (PO:0000282) absent on the inside of the fig (context: interior of the syconium). The fruit (PO:0009001) is present and glabrous or brown puberulous outside
fix: 'internal hairs absent', 'interfloral hairs absent' and 'hairs absent' mean that trichome PO:0000282 is absent at the stated position on the part. The part named before them is the context, never the absent entity.
reason: The phrase names hairs, not the fruit. Moving the absence to the fig is a wrong reading.

target: bract (PO:0009055) absent at a lateral position on the fig (fruit or syconium). The fruit is present and ribbed
fix: 'without <part>' following a part name puts the absence on the named part (here bract). The preceding organ is its context, never the absent entity.
reason: The absence was moved from the bracts to their bearer, the fig.

target: Waxy glands (portion of secretory tissue PO:0005656) absent from the leaf lamina, for example at the base of the midrib. The lamina (PO:0020039) is present and smooth
fix: 'glands absent', 'waxy glands absent' and 'glands 0' mean an absence of portion of secretory tissue PO:0005656 (or glandular trichome PO:0004509 when hairs are meant) on the part being described. Never move the absence to the part itself.
reason: Ficus leaves often bear waxy glands. Saying they are absent says nothing about the blade being absent.

target: No absence. The bracts (PO:0009055) are caducous, so they were not seen on the specimens. Keep only 'deciduous'
fix: 'not seen', 'not known', 'not observed' and 'unknown' after a part report a gap in the material. They are never an absence (PATO:0000462). Drop them.
reason: 'Bracts not seen' is explained by the bracts being caducous: they fall early.

target: Dots (pellucid or dark dots, no PO class) absent on the leaf lamina (PO:0020039). The lamina is present. Drop the statement or record it as a lamina without dots, if a value class is added later
fix: 'dots absent', 'punctations absent' and 'without dots' describe the surface of the lamina, never the absence of the lamina. If there is no class for dots, drop the statement rather than move the absence to the bearer.
reason: In Knema the lamina is described in detail. 'Dots' is a surface feature.

target: Dots absent on the leaf lamina (PO:0020039). Leaves (PO:0025034) are present. The 'raised' statement belongs to the leaf midvein (PO:0020139), not to the leaf
fix: Same rule as X02269: 'dots absent' is about a surface feature. In addition, 'midrib raised' should go to leaf midvein PO:0020139.
reason: The absence of a surface feature was moved to the whole leaf.

target: Glands (portion of secretory tissue PO:0005656) absent on the bract. The bract (PO:0009055) is present and concave
fix: 'glands absent' or 'eglandular' after a part means the part has no glands (PO:0005656). The part itself is never the absent entity.
reason: Trichosanthes bracts are described as glandular or not. The bract itself is there.

target: corona lobe (FLOPO:0986035) absent at the alternating positions. The corolla (PO:0009059) is present and glabrous inside
fix: 'corona lobes lacking' and 'corona absent' map to corona lobe FLOPO:0986035 (or the corona), never to the corolla. 'alternating' and 'inner' are position words that stay as the context.
reason: In Wrightia the corona is separate from the corolla. Only one set of corona lobes is missing.

target: rosette leaf (PO:0000014) absent. The cauline leaves (PO:0000013) are present, sessile or shortly petiolate
fix: 'no basal leaves', 'basal leaves absent', 'without basal rosette' and 'basal leaves withered at flowering' are about rosette leaf PO:0000014 only. Never record a general leaf absence.
reason: The modifier 'basal' was lost, which turned the statement into a taxon-wide leaf absence.

target: disk flower (PO:0025332) absent. The heads have only ray (ligulate) flowers, and flowers (PO:0009046) are present
fix: 'no disk florets', 'disk florets absent' and 'rays absent' map to disk flower PO:0025332 or ray flower PO:0025331. They never mean flower PO:0009046 absent.
reason: Sonchus heads are all ligulate. Only the disk florets are absent.

target: The apical peg (beak) of the fruit is absent. There is no PO class for it, so drop the statement or record it as fruit apex without a beak. The fruit (PO:0009001) is present and ovate
fix: 'apical peg absent', 'beak absent' and 'stipe absent' are the absence of an appendage or region of the part. If no class exists for it, drop the statement and never move the absence to the bearer.
reason: The fruit is described, so it is present. Only its peg is missing.

target: pistillode (PO:0009078) absent in the male flowers. The ovary (plant ovary PO:0009072) of the functional flowers is present and ovoid
fix: 'rudimentary ovary absent', 'pistillode absent' and 'ovary rudimentary or absent' in a male-flower paragraph map to pistillode PO:0009078, with the male flower as the context. Never use plant ovary for them.
reason: 'Rudimentary ovary' is the pistillode of male flowers. It is a different structure from the ovary.

target: rosette leaf (PO:0000014) absent. The cauline leaves (PO:0000013) are present and sessile
fix: 'without basal leaf rosette', 'rosette absent' and 'not forming a rosette' are about rosette leaf PO:0000014 (or the rosette PO:0025615). They never mean leaf absent.
reason: The rosette is missing, but the stem bears sessile leaves.

target: leaf (PO:0025034) decreased amount (PATO:0001997): the plant has few, reduced leaves, which are linear
fix: 'nearly leafless', 'almost leafless', 'subaphyllous' and 'subleafless' describe a quantity (decreased amount PATO:0001997). They are never an absence.
reason: The species name 'subaphyllum' means nearly leafless, and the leaves are described as linear.

target: domatium (FLOPO:0986021) absent. The leaf lamina (PO:0020039) is present and glossy above
fix: 'domatia absent', 'without domatia' and 'domatia 0' map to domatium FLOPO:0986021. They never mean that the part bearing them (lamina, leaf) is absent.
reason: Domatia sit on the lower surface of the lamina. Their absence says nothing about the lamina.
